The field moved from single-axis splitting (2017–19) to fixed 3D recipes with a "bandwidth-hungriest dimension innermost" placement rule (2020–21). It then added a sequence/context axis (2022–24) and EP as a first-class axis, and finally allowed *per-layer-type* mappings (folding, 2025–26). Across the same period, the "innermost" domain grew from one 8-GPU server to a 72-GPU rack (claims 10, 17, 26–27, 34–39).

**In scope:** how tensor (TP), pipeline (PP), context/sequence (CP/SP), expert (EP), and data (DP/FSDP/ZeRO) parallelism compose. That covers how the dimensions are ordered and placed on the network topology, the constraints between them, and where the usual placement rules stop holding.

**Out of scope:** single-dimension internals that don't involve composition, including kernel details, optimizer-state sharding theory, MoE router design beyond how it interacts with placement, and inference serving systems in general. Those are sibling or parent frontier items.
